senses.gloss: call. Sifra Vayikra, Par. 1 (ref. to Lev. I, 1) הקדים ק׳ לדיבור the Lord sent the call in advance of the speech.
units: <cite ref="Leviticus 1:1">Ib.</cite> <he>על כל ק׳ הוא אומר הנני</he> to every call he responded with ‘here am I.’ <cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 11">Deut. R. s. 11</cite>, beg. <he>חתם יצחק בק׳</he> Isaac closed his blessings with a call (<cite ref="Genesis 28:1">Gen. XXVIII, 1</cite>); <he>אני … אלא בק׳</he> I will commence with a call (ib. XLIX, 1); a. fr.

senses.gloss: reading esp. from the Scriptures. קְרִיאַת שמע (קְרִיַּת) (abbrev. ק״ש), or ק׳ (sub. שמע) the recitation of Sh’mʿa (Deut. VI, 4-9; XI, 13-21; Num. XV, 37-41) in the morning and in the evening prayer.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 13b:11">Ber. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>מצות ק׳</he> the duty of reciting, contrad. to <he>מצות כונה</he>, v. <cite ref="K00303"><he>כַּוָּנָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Berakhot 13b:11">Ib.</cite> <he>זו ק״ש של ר׳ וכ׳</he> this (the verse <cite ref="Deuteronomy 6:4">Deut. VI, 4</cite>) was all that R. Judah han-Nasi read (when engaged in teaching); a. fr.—V. <cite ref="U01513"><he>שְׁמַע</he> II</cite>.—<he>קריאת המגלה</he> the recitation of the Book of Esther.

<cite ref="Makkot 18b:10">Macc. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>הראויין לק׳</he> those first-fruits which are fit for reciting over them (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 26:3">Deut. XXVI, 3</cite> sq.); a. fr.—Pl. <he>קְרִיאוֹת</he>, <he>קְרִיּוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 4:1">Deut. R. s. 4</cite>, beg. <he>מהו לקרות … בק׳ הרבה</he> how about reading ‘the reproofs’ (<cite ref="V00202"><he>תּוֹכָחָה</he></cite>) by several calls (by calling up several persons successively).

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 4:1">Ib.</cite> <he>אם יקראו … ק׳ הרבה וכ׳</he> if they do read … by several calls, each called-up person should not recite the benediction before and after &c.—Cmp. <cite ref="S01941"><he>קְרוּיוֹת</he></cite>.
